verdicts.correction: Re-run 2026-10-24 ~11:15Z with no cookie: POST /v1/authentication-ticket (with and without the trailing slash, body {} or none), /v1/logout, /v2/logout and GET /v1/client-assertion/ all return 401 {code 9002, subcode 0, 'Authentication token is missing'}. None sends an x-csrf-token. The rate limit is 1000/60s on each. The '403 + x-csrf-token when a valid cookie is sent' half comes only from RAM's GetCSRFToken (Account.cs lines 134-160, verified). I could not test it. One nuance: some other hosts (friends.roblox.com, apis.roblox.com) run the CSRF check BEFORE the auth check. A no-cookie POST there returns 403 with a token, but it is the shared guest token and does not prime a session.

The shared-store and retry-on-403 design in CoreUtilities.js is verified (oQ='x-csrf-token', localStorage, storeCRSFToken). One correction to 'needs no TTL': tokens DO expire. The no-cookie guest token the researcher saw (9BPntHEa3vgM, 10:47-11:05Z) had been replaced by ~11:22Z. The new token, cfv6TgzPf32Q, was identical on auth.roblox.com, apis.roblox.com, friends.roblox.com and the page meta csrf-token, and the old value is now rejected with 403 plus a new token. So tokens rotate on a time window of tens of minutes or less. The client strategy (cache, retry once on 403 + header) is right; never assume a cached token is still valid. That the token is bound to the cookie session is still inferred.

Verified: auth.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 returns 404. users.roblox.com/docs/json/v1 302-redirects to prod.docsiteassets.roblox.com. auth/v1.json has Last-Modified Fri, 23 Oct 2026 19:09:02 GMT, lists GET /v1/client-assertion (tag AuthenticationTicket, GetClientAssertionResponse {clientAssertion}), and has no authentication-ticket or redeem paths. v1 also lists /v1/logoutfromallsessionsandreauthenticate and /v1/session/refresh. v3 has only /v3/logout (LogoutV3Request {logoutReason,url,userId}) and /v3/users/{userId}/two-step-verification/login.

Both code paths in GameLaunch.js are verified: rb() and the legacy er.get/er.post path both call GET /v1/client-assertion/, then POST /v1/authentication-ticket/ with content-type application/json and body = assertion ?? {}, then read rbx-authentication-ticket. Minor: RAM master (Account.cs:118) sends the POST with no body at all, while fork issue #8 describes v3.7.2 as sending 'an empty JSON body'. Whether {} or an empty body is still accepted server-side is unverified.

The Referer requirement rests on a 2022 thread. The 2025-2026 searches found nothing current about 'UrlReferrer was invalid', and the Origin requirement is untestable without a cookie. The redeem probe is verified: 403 code 4 'Authentication ticket was invalid.', rate limit 50/60s. Sending a www.roblox.com Referer and Origin is cheap and harmless, so keep it, but treat 'required' as unconfirmed.

Verified from the saved page: 49 whitelist entries (all '100' except jQuery '1000000'), exemptlist empty, and hbaDB/hbaObjectStore/hba_keys/version 1, bat-event-sample-rate 500. 'hbaDB' is also the hard-coded prod default inside CoreUtilities ('hbaDb-Test'/'hbaObjStore-Test'/'hba-keys' for test), so the roblox-bat README's 'hbaStore' is simply outdated. The whitelist is NOT used by the attach predicate. The predicate pY only checks signed-in, the host suffix (.roblox.com/.robloxlabs.com/.roblox.qq.com), the non-empty DB names and isBoundAuthTokenEnabled. The jQuery entry is a per-userId rollout (userId % 1e6 < sampleRate). apis.roblox.com is not in the whitelist but is still signed via the domain allowlist.

One small correction: generateKey is called with usages ['sign','verify'], not ['sign'], with extractable=false, so the key is non-extractable as stated. Verified: the signed strings are [bodyHash,ts,url,METHOD].join('|') and ['',ts,path,METHOD].join('|'), and the header is ['v1',bodyHash,ts,sig1,sig2].join('|'). The nonce comes from apis.roblox.com/hba-service/v1/getServerNonce, which is live unauthenticated, returns a JSON string such as "DGJXG7B6KB94FTBM" and is limited to 50/60s. Also present: a cross-subdomain path in which pages postMessage 'signSubdomainRequest' to an iframe that holds the key and receive back batHeader['x-bound-auth-token'].

Still unconfirmed for BAT specifically, but the researcher missed stronger staff evidence. In the ASP thread on 2025-02-14, ttaahw wrote that breaking changes are deferred, the 'enforcement schedule and list of affected endpoints is being refreshed, and no changes are required from developers at this moment'. On 2026-05-27, ChemexWizard (Roblox Staff) wrote that 'workflows that use .ROBLOSECURITY cookies will be unaffected' and that ASP 'will continue to help secure accounts in the background … as a security signal to help detect suspicious activity'. So hard rejection of unsigned requests is officially NOT in force as of 2026-05. An unbound or unsigned use may still feed risk scoring, so expect challenges rather than hard 401s. The 9002/2 predicate in CoreUtilities is verified. The roblox-bat README also says the library is unnecessary if login did not include secureAuthenticationIntent.

This claim is stale. The 2023-10/2024-02 plan (enforce on auth.roblox.com etc. by June 2024, with an opt-out in Creator Hub > Settings > Advanced) never shipped as announced. In post 189 (2025-02-14, ttaahw), breaking changes were deferred and the endpoint list and schedule were being 'refreshed', and users could opt back in via 'Standard Protection'. In post 191 (2026-05-27, ChemexWizard, Roblox Staff), 'The "No protection" opt-out setting is being removed'. Opted-out accounts are 'rolled back into a standard protection behavior with no interruption to existing cookie support', cookie-based workflows are 'unaffected', and ASP is now a background security signal. So no opt-out toggle exists today, and there is no announced endpoint enforcement.

Verified in the thread JSON. OP by ttaahw is dated 2026-02-03 (edited 2026-02-19). The date 'on or after 1 May 2026', the Set-Cookie wording, the regex and staff reply #12 'Exactly right!' all match. Staff post #22 adds that cookies 'may have breaking updates without specific notice from May 1, 2026 onwards'. The last post was 2026-08-01, and there are no later staff updates.
The redeem probe is reconfirmed (403 code 4, 50/60s). No primary source was found on ticket lifetime, single use, or whether redemption affects the issuing cookie.

Only user reports exist. More 2024 user reports in the ASP thread (posts 184-187, 2024-09/10) describe .ROBLOSECURITY 'resets' when the cookie is used from an external host, even with ASP off, and another user attributes it to an out-of-region IP. Staff have never confirmed IP or region binding. The 2026-05 staff post says ASP acts as a 'security signal', which is consistent with risk-based invalidation but does not state it.

The builder is verified (pY/pZ): the separator is '+', '1' comes first, gameinfo is encodeURIComponent(ticket), and the params are added in this order: placelauncherurl, browsertrackerid, robloxLocale, gameLocale, channel (omitted on Win/Mac when the flag is set), LaunchExp. Notes: (1) the pG default protocolNameForClient is 'roblox-client', overwritten at document.ready with p3('roblox-player'), and p3 can add a '-sitetest3'-style suffix on test environments. (2) data-protocol-player-channel-name is 'LIVE', and 'LIVE' is mapped to an empty channel, so non-Win/Mac platforms get 'channel:'. (3) The live example is simplified: on the legacy jQuery.param path, which is the one active today, the PlaceLauncher query may carry empty keys (launchData=&eventId=&referredByPlayerId=) depending on the caller.

Re-probed. assetgame /game/PlaceLauncher.ashx gives 301 to /request-error?code=404. www GET gives the generic 404 HTML page, and www POST gives 404 JSON {errors:[{code:0,message:''}]}. pJ() uses getAbsoluteUrl('/Game/PlaceLauncher.ashx'). Correction: the 404 HTML is not byte-identical across requests (67,100 vs 67,929 bytes in my probes; it embeds a per-request machine-id). It is the same generic 404 page, so the conclusion holds. That the client only parses the URL's query remains an inference.

Verified in GameLaunch.js: there are request types for RequestGame, RequestGameJob, RequestPrivateGame, RequestFollowUser and RequestPlayTogetherGame. The deep-link path calls joinPrivateGame({placeId, linkCode}) with no accessCode, and the server-list path builds {placeId, accessCode, linkCode}. isJoinAttemptIdEnabled is forced true. Only 'PlayButton', 'JoinInstance' and 'JoinUser' appear in GameLaunch.js; 'ServerListJoin' and 'privateServerJoin' would come from the ServerList bundle, which I did not re-check.

Verified. The deeplinks doc says 'This process is deprecated. To create public deep links, use share links.' gamejoin POST /v1/join-game without a cookie returns 200 status 12, but the message number varies ('Unable to join Game 211' today vs 212). join-game-instance returns 401 9002/0, and both are limited to 5 per 1 s. matchmaking-api client-status returns 200 {success:false}.

Confirmed: Bloxstrap StartRoblox uses FileName=executable and Arguments=_launchCommandLine (the raw URI); LaunchSettings accepts the 'roblox:' and 'roblox-player:' prefixes; LaunchHandler checks the ROBLOX_singletonMutex mutex. Bloxstrap v2.10.0 (2025-10-01) removed multi-instance launching ('roblox broke it'). The MultiBloxy README independently names ROBLOX_singletonEvent. Not independently confirmed: the claim that the '--launch-to-tray' Run-key autostart process holds both handles. Fork issue #7 itself says this 'needs testing with two real clients'. Also, RAM still matches a '-b (\d+)' tracker flag on RobloxPlayerBeta command lines, which suggests older launch paths did pass flags.

Re-observed: auth.roblox.com responses carry 'Server: cloudflare' and a __cf_bm Set-Cookie (Domain=roblox.com), and give the identical 401 with curl's default UA. Other hosts answer with server: public-gateway. Whether Cloudflare challenges authenticated non-browser traffic is still unknown.

Re-observed per-route limits with no cookie: authentication-ticket 1000/60, logout v1/v2 1000/60, client-assertion 1000/60, redeem 50/60, getServerNonce 50/60, gamejoin '5, 5;w=1', matchmaking client-status 100/60, and www/assetgame 100/60. The authenticated limits are still unknown.
rblx-challenge-id, -type and -metadata each appear 5 times in CoreUtilities.js, and generic-challenge-container appears 3 times. Whether authentication-ticket itself triggers challenges is unknown.

The GameLaunch parser is verified: pi() matches /browserid=([^&]*)/i against RBXEventTrackerV2. In my no-cookie probes of www.roblox.com /home, /games/1818 and /XsrfToken at ~11:22Z, the server set only rbx-ip2 and GuestData, not RBXEventTrackerV2. The researcher's fixture redacts the value, so the '16-digit' format cannot be confirmed. pealz1 issue #1 (2026-10-03, closed the same day via PR #6) proposes rules, not regexes: place ids ASCII digits, job ids letters/digits/dashes, link codes 'letters and digits'. The design implication's linkCode ^[0-9]+$ is therefore stricter than any source supports. Use ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$ (or digits plus a fallback) to avoid rejecting valid codes.

missed.claim: Account Session Protection: the opt-out was removed on 2026-05-27, and enforcement was officially deferred in 2025-02. Staff say cookie workflows are unaffected and ASP is now a background 'security signal'.
missed.detail: Post 189 (ttaahw, 2025-02-14): breaking changes deferred; the 'enforcement schedule and list of affected endpoints is being refreshed, and no changes are required from developers at this moment'; users can opt back in via 'Standard Protection'. Post 191 (ChemexWizard, Roblox Staff, 2026-05-27): 'The "No protection" opt-out setting is being removed'; accounts are rolled back to standard protection 'with no interruption to existing cookie support'; workflows using .ROBLOSECURITY 'will be unaffected'; ASP is used 'as a security signal to help detect suspicious activity'. Design impact: do not tell users to opt out, because the option no longer exists. Expect risk-based challenges or invalidation rather than hard BAT 401s, and keep the 9002/2 and challenge detection.

missed.claim: Enhanced Protection (2026-04-21) makes passkeys or security keys mandatory for sign-in and 2SV on opted-in accounts.
missed.detail: From the DevForum post 'Introducing Enhanced Protection: Professional-Grade Security for Creators' (2026-04-21). With Enhanced Protection on, email OTP and authenticator codes are disabled for 2SV, and password or email-OTP sign-ins must also solve a passkey or hardware-key challenge. RoALT's 'add account' login must therefore run the real roblox.com login in WebView2, with WebAuthn/passkeys working. Any native username/password login path will fail for these accounts. Follow-up threads from June-July 2026 report lockouts after a passkey device was lost.

missed.claim: The CSRF token is shared across hosts but rotates on a short time window. Some hosts check CSRF before auth.
missed.detail: The no-cookie guest token changed from 9BPntHEa3vgM (10:47-11:05Z) to cfv6TgzPf32Q (~11:22Z). That value was identical on auth.roblox.com, apis.roblox.com, friends.roblox.com and the page meta csrf-token, and the old value is now rejected. friends.roblox.com POST /v1/users/1/request-friendship with no cookie returned 403 with a token (CSRF before auth), whereas auth.roblox.com authentication-ticket returns 401 first. Implication: implement retry-once-on-403 generically for every host, and never rely on a primed token staying valid between bulk launches.

missed.claim: Instance tracking can use the client log files, as Bloxstrap's ActivityWatcher does.
missed.detail: Bloxstrap reads the newest file containing 'Player' in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs (created within ~15 s of launch). Join line: "[FLog::Output] ! Joining game", parsed by @"! Joining game '([0-9a-f\-]{36})' place ([0-9]+) at ([0-9\.]+)" to get jobId, placeId and IP. Other markers: "[FLog::Network] Replicator created: " (joined), "[FLog::Network] Time to disconnect replication data:" (disconnected), "[FLog::SingleSurfaceApp] leaveUGCGameInternal" (left). Private servers are detected via referral_page RequestPrivateGame. This complements recording PIDs at spawn for mapping account to instance.

missed.claim: ic3w0lf22 Roblox-Account-Manager is archived, so its code is a historical reference, not a current one.
missed.detail: Search results report that the repository is archived; its last release notes 'Fixed Invalid Authentication Ticket error' in 3.7.2. Active follow-up work is in forks such as ethanstoner/Roblox-Account-Manager, whose 2026-09 issues are untested ('needs-account-test'). RAM master still builds assetgame PlaceLauncher URLs, sends 'channel:' empty, uses HttpUtility.UrlEncode ('+' for spaces, unlike encodeURIComponent), sends no body to authentication-ticket, and posts gamejoin v1/join-game-instance directly for small-server joins.

missed.claim: The web Account Switcher (up to 5 accounts per browser, stored on the device) is live, so one WebView2 profile can swap .ROBLOSECURITY between accounts.
missed.detail: The page has <meta name='account-switching-data' data-is-account-switching-enabled='true'>. The Help Center describes switching between up to five accounts from Settings and says the saved accounts are stored only on the device. If a user switches accounts inside an account's WebView2 profile, the captured cookie and the HBA key would belong to a different account. This supports the researcher's one-profile-per-account design, plus a check of users/v1/users/authenticated after any WebView session to confirm the cookie still maps to the expected userId.

missed.claim: MultiBloxy independently confirms that ROBLOX_singletonEvent is the singleton name current clients use, and that Roblox is actively blocking multi-instance tools.
missed.detail: The MultiBloxy README says Roblox uses ROBLOX_singletonEvent to keep a single instance running, and MultiBloxy creates it first. It warns that Roblox is actively blocking such tools. Clayell's Roblox-Multi-Instance-Script instead closes the handle via Sysinternals Handle. Together with Bloxstrap 2.10.0 removing multi-instance, the multi-instance feature should be treated as best-effort and kept behind a flag.
